tagline: Memory OS for a one-person Grok Bot company.

attribution.inspiredBy: KingWilliam, “How to build a one-person $1M company with Grok Bot”
attribution.note: Thesis credit only. Compound copy, prompts packaging, and starter pack are original. Do not treat this kit as a reprint of the article.

steps.title: Audit
steps.summary: See what each bot actually remembers before you change anything.
steps.why: Most one-person teams skip inventory. Private notes, shared facts, and leftover chat all sit in the same pile. An audit makes conflicts and missing context visible so you do not “fix” memory blind.
steps.pasteInto: A bot that can see your whole team (or run this once per bot and merge the answers).
steps.prompt: Look at every bot I run and show me what each one has in memory right now: what's private, what's shared, where two bots know conflicting things, and where a bot is missing context it clearly needs.

steps.title: Profile
steps.summary: Write a Who-I-Am card every bot reads before it acts.
steps.why: If the founder lives only in your head, every bot invents a slightly different you. A short shared profile — goals, standards, voice, hard nos — is the cheapest alignment layer you can install.
steps.pasteInto: Memory Steward, then confirm it landed in SHARED memory.
steps.prompt: Write a short "who I am" profile and save it to SHARED memory so every bot reads it before any task. Include: who I am, what I do, my goals this quarter, my standards, my tone of voice, and my hard nos. Keep it under 400 words.

steps.title: Interview
steps.summary: If the first draft is thin, let a bot interview you and write it.
steps.why: Blank-page profiles stay generic. Eight pointed questions about taste and intolerance produce a profile you will actually enforce. Save the result to shared memory, not the chat transcript.
steps.pasteInto: Memory Steward in a fresh thread.
steps.prompt: Ask me 8 questions about who I am and what I can't stand, then turn my answers into the profile and save it to shared memory.

steps.title: Split
steps.summary: Draw the shared vs private line, then re-file what is already wrong.
steps.why: Winners with the same bots and budget are usually better at this split. Facts about you, customers, tools, and decisions are company memory. Scratch notes on one task stay private. Mixed piles are how bots contradict each other.
steps.prompt: Set a memory rule for the team. Anything true about ME and my work (voice, customers, tools, rules, decisions) goes to SHARED. Anything that's one bot's notes on a single task stays PRIVATE. Re-sort anything already saved in the wrong place.

steps.title: Scope
steps.summary: One sentence of job. One sentence of never.
steps.why: A bot without a hard edge will “helpfully” touch money, posting, or another bot’s lane. Scope is memory, not a vibe. Lock job and prohibition on that bot so later skills cannot widen it quietly.
steps.pasteInto: Each role bot, once. Pick roles from the archive if you still need the seat filled.
steps.prompt: For each bot, lock in a one-sentence job and one clear line of what it must never do or touch. Save both to that bot's memory.

steps.title: Skills
steps.summary: Reusable teaching becomes a named skill, not another chat scrap.
steps.why: Chat is a graveyard. If you taught a procedure once, it should have a name, a file, and a reuse path. Browse the public archive for role skills, then teach only what is uniquely yours.
steps.pasteInto: The bot you are training. Then list what it claims to have saved.
steps.prompt: When I teach you something reusable, save it as a named skill I can reuse, not just a message in this chat. List the skills you've saved so far.

steps.title: Decisions
steps.summary: Start a DECISIONS log. Bots read it. They do not reopen it quietly.
steps.why: Without a log, every bot re-litigates pricing, positioning, and process. Write what you chose and why into shared memory. Acting against a logged decision should require a flag, not a shrug.
steps.pasteInto: Memory Steward. Use the DECISIONS template in this kit if you need a blank page.
steps.prompt: Start a DECISIONS log in shared memory. Every time I decide something, save what I chose and why. Read it before acting, and never reopen a logged decision without flagging me first.

steps.title: Rules
steps.summary: A correction becomes always X, never Y — for every bot.
steps.why: Correcting one bot in one thread trains a single conversation. Promoting the correction to a standing rule is how the company learns. Format matters: always / never is searchable and enforceable.
steps.pasteInto: Memory Steward, then spot-check a different bot.
steps.prompt: From now on, when I correct any bot, save it as a standing rule in the format "always X, never Y", and apply it across every bot, not just the one I corrected.

steps.title: Draft
steps.summary: Send, post, or spend only after you approve. Edits become rules.
steps.why: Draft-first is how a one-person company stays fast without leaking. The learning loop is the edit: capture why you changed the draft so the next one arrives closer. Approval is not bureaucracy; it is the training signal.
steps.pasteInto: Any bot that emails, posts, invoices, or spends.
steps.prompt: For anything that sends, posts, or spends, work in draft and wait for my approval. When I edit your draft, save WHY I changed it as a rule, so you get it right without me next time.

steps.title: Kill drift
steps.summary: Wrong facts do not get a second life. Delete, then rule.
steps.why: Memory drift is usually a leftover, not a personality. Find the bad store, delete it, write the correct rule. If you only correct in chat, the old version will resurface next week.
steps.pasteInto: The bot that just repeated the error, then Memory Steward.
steps.prompt: You just repeated something wrong. Find where that's stored in memory, delete it, and save the correct version as a rule so it can't resurface.

steps.title: Weekly
steps.summary: Learned / promote / stale — and nothing is deleted without a yes.
steps.why: Shared memory rots if nobody prunes. A weekly three-part review is the operating cadence: what was learned, what has earned a promotion to shared, what should die. You keep the delete key.
steps.pasteInto: Memory Steward on a standing weekly thread.
steps.prompt: Once a week show me three things: what you learned, what should be promoted to shared, and what's stale and should be deleted. Wait for my yes before deleting.

steps.title: Standing goal
steps.summary: Make cleanliness a /goal, not a mood.
steps.why: The last step is the one that keeps the other eleven from decaying. A standing goal tells the steward to prune, promote, and kill bad facts without waiting for you to remember the ritual.
steps.pasteInto: Memory Steward. Confirm the /goal is visible on that bot.
steps.prompt: /goal keep our memory clean and current on your own. Every week prune what's stale, promote what's proven to shared, and the moment I correct a fact, delete the wrong version so it can never come back.
